old: Dipole moment measures the polarity of a bond or molecule. It equals the magnitude of charge multiplied by the distance between the charges. It is a vector, drawn by chemists from the positive to the negative end, and its unit is the debye. The net molecular dipole is the vector sum of bond dipoles and lone pair contributions. Symmetrical molecules have zero dipole moment even with polar bonds: $CO_2$, $BF_3$, $CH_4$, $CCl_4$, $PCl_5$, $SF_6$ and $XeF_4$. $H_2O$ (1.85 D) and $NH_3$ (1.47 D) are polar. $NH_3$ has a larger dipole than $NF_3$ (0.23 D): in $NH_3$ the lone pair moment adds to the N–H bond moments, while in $NF_3$ it opposes the N–F moments. Applications include deciding polarity and geometry, distinguishing cis and trans isomers, and calculating percent ionic character. Polarity also follows functional groups. For example, $CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3 < CH_3COCH_3 < CH_3CH_2OH < CH_3COOH$.
new: Dipole moment measures the polarity of a bond or molecule. It equals the magnitude of charge multiplied by the distance between the charges. It is a vector, drawn by chemists from the positive to the negative end, and its unit is the debye. The net molecular dipole is the vector sum of bond dipoles and lone pair contributions. Symmetrical molecules have zero dipole moment even with polar bonds: $CO_2$, $BF_3$, $CH_4$, $CCl_4$, $PCl_5$, $SF_6$ and $XeF_4$. $H_2O$ (1.85 D) and $NH_3$ (1.47 D) are polar. $NH_3$ has a larger dipole than $NF_3$ (0.23 D): in $NH_3$ the lone pair moment adds to the N–H bond moments, while in $NF_3$ it opposes the N–F moments. Applications include deciding polarity and geometry, distinguishing cis and trans isomers, and calculating percent ionic character. Polarity also follows functional groups, in the sense NEET uses it (polarity as reflected by hydrogen bonding and interaction with polar media). For example, $CH_3CH_2OCH_2CH_3 < CH_3COCH_3 < CH_3CH_2OH < CH_3COOH$. By dipole moment alone, acetone (about 2.9 D) is higher than ethanol (about 1.7 D). Boiling points follow the same ether < ketone < alcohol < acid order.
fixes: Clarify NEET-sense polarity order vs dipole moment; boiling points follow same order
